subject: Re: Kickoff: CANN - M2 status: scale test in, memory is the story
body:
M2 status, couple days early since the numbers are stable.

M1 recap: run.sh end-to-end flow reproduced on the sample data (the Mapillary sanity set caught a real path bug, worth keeping in CI), Baidu-Mall results match the paper.

Scale test on the 10x internal capture set: recall@1 holds up well - we lose 2.3 points vs. the small-index regime, which Quentin says is in line with ANN scaling folklore. Query latency is fine: p50 41ms, p95 87ms on the 64-vCPU pool.

The story is memory: the index at 10x is 118GB resident, and the growth looks close to linear in total feature count. For the logistics pilot (their site survey is ~4x our test set again) that's approaching half-a-TB per site, which changes the serving hardware conversation entirely. Options we'll cost out for M3: feature subsampling per image (cheap, recall cost unknown), PQ-style compression on the vectors (CANN is feature-agnostic so nothing structural blocks it), or sharding per mall wing.

No schedule risk to M3 yet.

Linnea
